newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotels seeks casino license in Detroit.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotels seeks casino license in Detroit.

text.p: Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc said Wednesday that the it intends to apply for a license to operate a casino hotel in Detroit.
Voters in that city approved legalized gambling last November, after rejecting casinos on several previous occasions. Three casino licenses are expected to be awarded before the end of the year.
Trump Hotels owns three casinos in Atlantic City and a riverboat casino on Lake Michigan, near Buffington Harbor, Indiana.
The company said that chief executive Donald Trump will meet with local leaders June 19 to discuss the project and its place in the redevelopment of the city.
"We look forward to working together with these officials and hope to offer ideas and some solutions to help them continue in this outstanding job," Trump said in a statement.

President Nicholas Ribis said that he believes the company has an edge over its competitors because Trump's experience as a builder of commercial and residential buildings, not just as a casino operator, will be helpful in Detroit.
"We will add a real estate development expertise in addition to the casino that the other companies don't have," said Ribis.

Several other casino operators have either already applied, or expressed an interest in developing casino properties in the city, including Mirage Resorts Inc Harrah's Entertainment, Detroit buisnessman Don Barden, who operates the Majestic Star casino in Gary, Ind, and a group of local businessmen, Greektown Casino LLC.
The company said Detroit will issue its first guidelines for the project June 20, and will ask for responses by July 28.

Trump added that he proposed to take on a local partner for the project, Mel Farr, who he said is the largest African-American auto dealer in the country, with sales of $500 million in 1996 through 14 franchises in five states. Farr will have an equity interest in the proposed project.
